title: IMF tells Sri Lanka to focus on remainder of EFF program | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 16 October 2026 00:00
-     - 15

IMF Asia and Pacific Department Deputy Division Chief Sonali Jain-Chandra

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) yesterday urged Sri Lanka to stay focused on completing the ongoing Extended Fund Facility (EFF) program, which has two reviews still to run. 

The comments come amid persistent debate over Sri Lanka’s IMF engagement beyond March 2027, when the EFF program ends. The Fund said Sri Lanka’s fiscal performance had outshone that of its peers, and left the decision on any follow-on arrangement to the Government.

“Let me step back for a second just to acknowledge first the important achievements that have been garnered in the context of the [EFF] program, which still has some months left. The program has been delivering very strongly. The macroeconomic situation has much improved, and in contrast to other countries, the fiscal performance is actually very strong,” IMF Asia and Pacific Department Deputy Division Chief Sonali Jain-Chandra told a press briefing at the Annual Meetings in Thailand yesterday.

She said the revenue ratio had doubled, the debt restructuring was largely complete, and growth had been positive for 11 consecutive quarters since the crisis. She also cited structural gains, particularly on governance, which she described as a core part of the program.

Jain-Chandra cautioned, however, that the program was not yet complete. IMF staff reached a staff-level agreement on the Seventh Review in early October, and the IMF Executive Board will consider it in the coming weeks. A further review mission will follow before the program expires in March 2027.

“There are still two reviews left, so important work remains in the current program. It is very important to keep focused on the macroeconomic stabilisation that is happening and to consolidate the reform gains,” she said.

She was responding to a Sri Lankan journalist who asked whether the IMF saw a need for a new arrangement, given that major debt repayments resume in 2028 and the country remains exposed to climate and oil shocks. Jain-Chandra said that decision rested with the authorities.

“There are many ways in which the Fund can support Sri Lanka, whether it is a new financing arrangement, granular policy advice in the context of surveillance, or capacity development, of which Sri Lanka is a very significant beneficiary. We stand ready to support Sri Lanka in any way the authorities desire, and the Fund will remain a very committed partner,” she said.

Elsewhere in South Asia, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast to 7% for this year and next, after a stronger-than-expected first quarter of its fiscal year. Bangladesh, by contrast, faces inflation of 8% and a revenue-to-GDP ratio of just 7%, among the lowest in the world. Jain-Chandra said Bangladesh needs tight monetary conditions and a credible plan to repair a very weak financial sector. Bangladesh requested a new IMF program in May.

For Asia and the Pacific as a whole, the IMF expects growth to ease from 5% in 2025 to 4.8% in 2026 and 4.4% in 2027. That is stronger than projected in April, and implies the region will account for more than two-thirds of global growth. IMF Asia and Pacific Department Director Krishna Srinivasan said the region had absorbed an energy shock that began in February, as well as the 2025 tariff increases, helped by a boom in artificial intelligence (AI)-related technology. He added that the benefits had been uneven.

“Asia’s growth is projected to slow, but continue to outpace the world. But resilience is not unlimited,” Srinivasan said. He pointed to limits on drawing down energy inventories and the mounting fiscal cost of relief measures.

He said risks were tilted to the downside. They include renewed escalation in the Middle East, a reassessment of AI-related profitability, higher sovereign borrowing costs, and a potentially exceptional El Niño cycle. Srinivasan urged central banks to safeguard price stability and their independence, and called on governments to rebuild fiscal buffers while shielding the vulnerable through targeted support.

“The idea is to protect people, not prices,” he said.

title: Half of earlier Port City approvals fall away, CoPF finds | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 16 October 2026 00:30
-     - 0

Half of the investors approved in an earlier round at Colombo Port City have withdrawn or are no longer proceeding, Parliament’s Committee on Public Finance (CoPF) was told. 

CoPF members questioned how the Colombo Port City Economic Commission (CPCEC) vets ambitious proposals before gazetting them. Reviewing 10 earlier approvals, CoPF Chairman MP Dr. Harsha de Silva said five had withdrawn and five remained in operation. 

Those he listed as no longer proceeding included the Asiri Port City Hospital and the Gateway International Campus. The CPCEC, chaired by Harsha Amarasekera, said some of the entities named had been in the pipeline but were never gazetted.

The most striking withdrawal was Clothespin Management and Development, which the CPCEC Director-General said was gazetted in July 2025. According to the Gazette as read by Dr. de Silva, the project promised a seven-star hotel, luxury residences, Grade A offices, retail space, and a vertical art gallery intended to win a Guinness World Record as the world’s largest art piece. 

Dr. de Silva questioned whether the Commission had found these plans credible. The CPCEC Director-General said the investor had informed the Commission it was not proceeding.

The exit cost the investor little. The Commission said the applicant had paid a $ 10,000 application fee, the standard fee for processing an application. Because the hotel plot sat on land leased to the Chinese project company, the investor is also believed to have forfeited a token deposit paid to that company. Members noted that the investor therefore lost only the fee to the Commission, despite the cost of processing and gazetting the project.

Universal Entertainment Colombo, which had considered a 10-hectare plot earmarked for an integrated resort under the Port City’s development control regulations, also withdrew during its due diligence. Dr. de Silva described it as a gaming and casino applicant.

The CPCEC Director-General was unable to identify two other names on the Committee’s list. He said one could be a secondary business or an authorised person rather than a primary developer, and he could not recall the other.

Of the earlier approvals, the developments proceeding include the mixed-use Colombo International Financial Centre, the Colombo Marina development, CIFC Colombo 1, and a residential project by ICC Port City. The Colombo International Financial Centre will comprise around 150,000 square metres of residential, commercial, and retail space, with piling under way. 

The ICC residential project has reached the first-floor stage, while work on the marina itself has begun. CIFC Colombo 1 is expected to start shortly. Amarasekera said the Colombo International Financial Centre involves Chinese construction worth $ 500 million, and that all other projects under way are Sri Lankan.

The Chairman defended the Commission’s record. He said the Port City had been bare land when the Commission first appeared before the Committee, and that nearly 10 parcels have since been leased with significant commitments on six more. Dr. de Silva acknowledged that progress but noted that groundwork had also been laid by previous commissions (See: https://www.ft.lk/front-page/Freehold-clause-rupee-pre-sales-and-BSI-ownership-test-Port-City-safeguards/44-798699).

title: ComBank partners Payable to introduce ‘Soundbox’ for small business digital payments | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 16 October 2026 00:26
-     - 18

Driven by its commitment to introduce the latest global technologies and continuously elevate the customer experience, Commercial Bank of Ceylon has announced the introduction of ‘Soundbox,’ an innovative audio-enabled digital payment acceptance device tailored for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). 

Powered by Mastercard and implemented in partnership with Payable Ltd., the Soundbox solution is designed to bring small and micro merchants, many of whom continue to rely predominantly on cash transactions, into the formal digital payments ecosystem through an affordable, simple, and efficient acceptance mechanism. 

These devices support acceptance across all major card networks and QR schemes available in the market, marking a significant milestone in the evolution of the country’s payment landscape.

Soundbox supports both contactless card payments and QR-based transactions, and provides real-time audio confirmation for every successful payment. The device announces each completed transaction, enabling merchants to verify payments instantly without interrupting their workflow. QR-based transactions will also benefit from immediate crediting, further enhancing liquidity for small businesses.

Commercial Bank Managing Director/CEO Sanath Manatunge said: “What makes this solution compelling is its ability to remove longstanding barriers to entry for small merchants by combining affordability with immediacy. By enabling instant onboarding, real-time transaction visibility, and multi-channel acceptance through a single device, we are equipping businesses with a practical tool to participate more competitively in an increasingly digital marketplace.”

Payable Co-Founder and CEO Yohan Wijesiriwardane explained: “At Payable, for over a decade, we have been building towards a single goal of ensuring that no merchant is left behind in Sri Lanka’s digital economy. Soundbox brings that vision to life. A small business owner who set up shop last week should have the same access to digital payments as the largest retailer in the country, and at a price point that makes sense for where they are today. That is what this partnership with Commercial Bank and Mastercard makes possible.”

Mastercard Country Manager – Sri Lanka Mahesha Amarasuriya said: “Mastercard’s focus is on driving secure, simple, and inclusive payment experiences empowering small businesses to thrive. The introduction of Soundbox with Commercial Bank and Payable is a significant step in expanding digital acceptance for Sri Lanka. Combining affordability with innovation, the milestone supports the country’s micro and small merchant ecosystem to embrace digital payments with confidence, strengthen financial inclusion and advance Sri Lanka’s journey toward a cash-lite economy.”

The Soundbox solution is particularly suited to merchants who have found traditional point-of-sale infrastructure costly or complex. By offering a significantly lower-cost alternative that combines multiple payment methods into a single device, Soundbox eliminates the need for multiple terminals while reducing checkout friction and improving operational efficiency.

The initiative reflects Commercial Bank’s continued leadership in digital innovation and its commitment to extending the benefits of secure, convenient, and inclusive financial services to underserved business segments. It also aligns with national priorities to accelerate digital adoption and reduce dependence on cash-based transactions.

Customers stand to benefit from faster, safer and more convenient payment experiences at neighbourhood businesses, while merchants gain access to reliable digital payment acceptance, reduced cash handling, enhanced transaction transparency and stronger customer trust. The introduction of Soundbox is expected to play a pivotal role in digitally empowering small businesses and deepening their integration into the formal financial system, the Bank said.

title: CSE green lights Sampath Bank’s Rs. 10 b debenture issue | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 16 October 2026 00:25
-     - 13

The Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) yesterday said it has approved in principle Sampath Bank PLC’s Rs. 10 billion debenture issue and subscriptions will open on 20 October.

The bank will initially offer 70 million Basel III-compliant, listed, rated, unsecured, subordinated, redeemable debentures with a non-viability conversion feature, at a par value of Rs. 100 each, amounting to Rs. 7 billion.

It may issue a further 30 million debentures at its discretion if the initial issue is oversubscribed, bringing the total to a maximum of Rs. 10 billion.

The issue comprises two types. Type A debentures carry a five-year tenor ending in 2031 at a fixed interest rate of 12.8% per annum, while Type B debentures have a seven-year tenor ending in 2033 at a fixed 13%. Interest on both is payable annually, with the annual effective rates matching the stated interest rates.

The bank’s Investor Relations Department is the Manager to the issue, Capital Alliance Partners Ltd., is the Placement Agent and Central Depository Systems Ltd., is the Registrar.

Soft copies of the prospectus were made available to trading participants yesterday.

title: Crevaty Co-Founder Dimuthu Ethugala named CA Sri Lanka Outstanding Global Achiever | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 16 October 2026 00:24
-     - 17

Dimuthu Ethugala (right) receiving the Outstanding Global Achiever of the Year 2026 award from CA Sri Lanka President Tishan Subasinghe

The Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (CA Sri Lanka) has named Crevaty Co-Founder Dimuthu Ethugala Outstanding Global Achiever of the Year 2026, recognising his international professional achievements, entrepreneurial leadership, and contribution to the profession.

The award was presented on 8 October at the 47th National Conference of Chartered Accountants at Monarch Imperial, Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte.

After starting his career at BDO Sri Lanka and KPMG in Kuwait, Ethugala established Crevaty in 2017 with fellow Chartered Accountants Sujeewa Appuhami and Jude Paththamperume. The firm, which began with accounting, taxation, and business advisory services, now operates across Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Singapore, the UK, and Canada, supported by delivery operations in Sri Lanka. It employs approximately 45 full-time professionals and generates annual revenue of around Rs. 500 million.

Between 2019 and 2023, Ethugala held several leadership positions at the CA Sri Lanka Kuwait Chapter, including President. A Fellow of CA Sri Lanka and CMA Sri Lanka, he mentors emerging professionals.

“More than an honour, it felt like a responsibility to give back to the profession and community that shaped me,” Ethugala said. 

He intends to strengthen Crevaty’s international presence while creating further opportunities for Sri Lankan professionals in global service delivery.

title: Manufacturing, services PMI stay in expansion zone in September | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 16 October 2026 00:23
-     - 22

The country’s manufacturing and services sectors in September have expanded, as per the Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI), its compiler the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) said. 

The Manufacturing PMI registered an index value of 53 in September, remaining unchanged compared to the previous month, indicating that manufacturing activities continued to expand at a similar pace during the month.

The CBSL said the expansion in New Orders and Production was largely attributed to positive developments in both the Food and Beverages and Textiles and Wearing Apparel manufacturing sectors.

Meanwhile, Employment continued to expand, albeit at a slower pace, in September. 

However, the Stock of Purchases moderated towards the neutral threshold, indicating broadly unchanged inventory levels during the month. Further, Suppliers’ Delivery Time remained lengthened during the month.

The CBSL said the outlook for manufacturing activities over the next three months remains positive, driven largely by optimism on year-end seasonal demand.

The Services PMI registered an index value of 60.5 in September, indicating an expansion in services activities, but at a slower rate compared to 65.6 in August.

Business activity increased in September, reflecting improvements across several subsectors, led by Financial Services, with notable contributions from Education and Professional Services.

New Businesses increased in September, primarily driven by the expansion in the Financial Services sector, with positive contributions from the Insurance, Education, Professional, and Other Personal Services subsectors.

Employment increased in September, as firms across several sectors increased recruitment to meet operational needs and support business expansion. Meanwhile, Backlogs of Work declined, although at a slower rate compared to the previous month.

The CBSL said expectations for business activity over the next three months continued to improve, supported by favourable macroeconomic conditions, increased tourist arrivals, and the upcoming festive season. However, broader global uncertainties continued to pose risks to the outlook.

title: Arugam Bay voted Asia’s best beach | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 16 October 2026 00:22
-     - 14

Arugam Bay has been ranked Asia’s best beach in the Condé Nast Traveller Readers’ Choice Awards 2026, one of four Sri Lankan beaches to make the region’s top 20.

The surfing destination on Sri Lanka’s eastern coast scored 98.84, the highest in the Asian rankings.

It finished ahead of Railay Beach in Thailand, which scored 94.44, and Coral Beach in Malaysia, which scored 93.33. Boracay in the Philippines and Nusa Dua Beach in Indonesia completed the top five.

Bentota Beach was placed ninth with a score of 88.33, Tangalle Beach 14th with 83.33 and Negombo Beach 19th with 78.92. Together, the four entries span different stretches of the island’s coastline.

title: Airlines representatives weigh cost pressures, ground handling reforms, airport upgrades | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 16 October 2026 00:21
-     - 18

The Board of Airline Representatives (BAR) Sri Lanka yesterday took up rising operating costs, ground handling procedures, and airport infrastructure at its fourth Executive Board meeting in Colombo.

The session, held at the SriLankan Airlines Boardroom, was chaired by BAR Chairman Dimuthu Tennakoon, along with Vice Chairman Sudesh Rupasinghe and country heads of major airlines serving Sri Lanka.

The representatives discussed ways to simplify ground handling processes, contain growing operational expenses, and improve facilities at the country’s main aviation gateways.

The Executive Committee also reviewed strategies to raise operational efficiency and to press for aviation policies that support the industry.

BAR Sri Lanka reaffirmed its commitment to sustainable growth in the sector, better passenger experiences, and support for the country’s tourism and trade industries.

title: Landmark hotel Galadari to reopen as Radisson Blu | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 16 October 2026 00:20
-     - 17

Galadari Hotels (Lanka) PLC said it will reopen its landmark Colombo hotel as the Radisson Blu Hotel Galadari Colombo in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The hotel, which has over 450 rooms overlooking Galle Face Green and the Indian Ocean, is undergoing refurbishment. 

The reopening will be scheduled once the renovation is complete, in line with the approval of Radisson Hospitality Belgium BV under the Hotel Management Agreement, the company said.

Galadari Hotels entered into a Hotel Development Services Agreement and a Hotel Management Agreement with Radisson Hotel Asia Pacific Investments Ltd., in 2023.
